title: Fall Ball Wrap: Texas A&M Goes a Perfect 6-0, Tops Defending Champion Texas 7-1 to Close the Fall
excerpt: Texas A&M closed out fall ball with a perfect 6-0 record, beating back-to-back national champion Texas 7-1 on Friday at Davis Diamond, while Michigan stayed unbeaten and Arizona reshuffled its fall schedule ahead of signing day.
content:
Texas A&M closed out its fall softball schedule in style, beating Texas 7-1 on Friday at Davis Diamond in front of 2,425 fans to finish fall ball with a perfect 6-0 record. The Aggies scored seven unanswered runs against the two-time defending national champions.

The win capped a fall in which Texas A&M outscored its opponents 63-12, with victories over Murray State College, Temple College, McLennan Community College, Texas State, Grayson College and Texas. The Aggies entered Friday's finale 5-0, having already outscored their first five opponents 56-11.

Texas, meanwhile, used the fall to blood its newcomers. The Longhorns swept Texas Tech 7-3 and 4-1 in June to win back-to-back Women's College World Series titles, with ace Teagan Kavan earning Most Outstanding Player honors for the second straight year, the first two-time MOP in WCWS history. Head coach Mike White has spent the fall giving freshmen reps at different positions, with 18 batters, including six freshmen, getting at least one plate appearance in an exhibition against McLennan Community College.

Around the country, Michigan also wrapped up an undefeated fall. The Wolverines, led by All-American Lauren Putz, who batted .435 with 22 home runs and 80 RBI last spring, improved their fall team batting average from .302 to .432 against largely the same competition as a year ago. Arizona State opened its fall with a 4-4 tie against Grand Canyon after keeping just nine players from last season's Super Regional team and adding 17 newcomers.

Arizona adjusted its fall schedule after weather wiped out games last weekend, adding Red-Blue scrimmages on November 6 and 7 and another on November 12, plus a matchup against UNLV on November 13. Florida State, the only team in the country returning two All-American pitchers in Ashtyn Danley and Jazzy Francik, closes its fall at Florida on November 13. Arizona also begins signing its 2027 recruiting class on Wednesday, November 11.

The regular season begins in February 2027, when the fall work turns into real games.

Sources: Texas A&M Athletics; NCAA.com; The Daily Texan; Line Drive Media; Arizona Desert Swarm; Florida State Athletics.
